paragraphs.text: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 is an autosomal recessive disorder. It presents with severe thrombocytopenia and markedly reduced bone marrow megakaryocytes, which can progress to trilineage bone marrow failure (Seo et al., 2017; Pecci et al., 2018). The bone marrow failure does not respond to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, but patients have responded to THPO receptor agonists (Seo et al., 2017; Pecci et al., 2018; Capaci et al., 2023).

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) reported 3 sibs with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia, born to Egyptian parents who were first cousins. The proband, a boy, presented at 3.5 years of age with ecchymoses. He had very severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 3 x 10(9)/l), hyporegenerative anemia, and severe neutropenia. Bone marrow was hypocellular with very rare immature megakaryocytes, and the karyotype was normal. He also had preauricular skin tags and a left divergent squint. After Fanconi anemia and PNH were excluded, he was initially diagnosed with idiopathic aplastic anemia. He went on to have recurrent major hemorrhages and severe infections that required multiple transfusions. His brother had severe isolated thrombocytopenia (26 x 10(9)/l) at 7 months of age, with markedly reduced bone marrow megakaryocytes, and developed recurrent spontaneous bleeding at 1.6 years. A younger sister developed a hematoma at a vaccination site at 2 months of age and was found to have anemia and severe thrombocytopenia. Platelet size and blood cell morphology were normal. Because the oldest sib had trilineage hypoplasia, Pecci et al. (2018) suggested that the hematologic picture worsens with age. They noted that the phenotype could not be distinguished from CAMT caused by MPL mutations.

paragraphs.text: Capaci et al. (2023) reported a boy born to consanguineous Muslim Palestinian parents who were first cousins. He came to medical attention at 3.5 years with easy bruising and thrombocytopenia (21 x 10(9)/L), and his mean platelet volume was normal. His platelet count shortly after birth had been 70 x 10(9)/L. At age 2 years, when he was diagnosed with urethral stenosis, he had severe thrombocytopenia (20 x 10(9)/L). Bone marrow was normocellular, with severe megakaryocyte hypoplasia and mild dyserythropoiesis. Apart from mild occasional neutropenia, he had no other cytopenias. Chromosomal breakage analysis excluded Fanconi anemia.

paragraphs.text: Dasouki et al. (2013), Seo et al. (2017), Pecci et al. (2018), and Capaci et al. (2023) established autosomal recessive inheritance of CAMT2: affected individuals were homozygous for THPO mutations. Heterozygous carriers can have mild thrombocytopenia. In the family reported by Dasouki et al. (2013), both heterozygous parents and a heterozygous sib had reduced platelet counts. In the family reported by Capaci et al. (2023), the heterozygous mother and younger sib of the homozygous proband had asymptomatic mild thrombocytopenia. The mother's count was around 80 x 10(9)/L and worsened during pregnancies, and the sib's count was 130 x 10(9)/L at birth. Capaci et al. (2023) considered this consistent with mild thrombocytopenia in carriers of monoallelic THPO loss-of-function variants.

paragraphs.text: In 2 Micronesian sibs with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2013) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.112C-T mutation in the THPO gene. The mutation results in an arg38-to-cys (R38C) substitution in the receptor-binding domain; excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide, it is designated R17C. In silico modeling predicted that the introduced fifth cysteine may disrupt normal disulfide bonding among the 4 conserved cysteines of the receptor-binding domain and impair receptor binding. Media containing the mutant THPO had a 2- to 3-fold reduced ability to sustain proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells. The authors concluded that the mutation is a partial loss-of-function allele.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) sequenced MPL and THPO in an Egyptian proband with CAMT and found no MPL variants. They identified a homozygous c.355C-T variant in THPO, resulting in an arg119-to-cys (R119C) substitution. The variant segregated with the disease: both affected sibs were also homozygous, and the parents were heterozygous. It was absent from the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, and ExAC databases, and most in silico tools predicted it to be pathogenic. In transfected HEK293T cells, the mutant was expressed at levels similar to or higher than wildtype and was equally stable. However, its concentration in culture supernatants was about 23-fold lower, indicating impaired secretion. Tested at equal concentrations, the mutant had about 50% of wildtype activity in stimulating proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells and in activating STAT5, ERK1/2, and AKT. The previously reported R38C mutant behaved similarly.

paragraphs.text: By whole-exome sequencing in a Palestinian boy with CAMT, Capaci et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.-323C-T substitution in the promoter region of the THPO gene, 45 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site. The parents and a younger sib were heterozygous, and 2 healthy sibs were homozygous wildtype. The variant was in dbSNP but not in gnomAD, and it lies in a region conserved across species. No variants were found in MPL, MECOM, HOXA11, RBM8A, or other bone marrow failure genes. The variant abolished predicted ETS1 and STAT4 binding sites. In luciferase assays in HEK293T cells, the mutant promoter reduced reporter activity by almost 80%. Silencing ETS1 and/or STAT4 reduced the activity of the wildtype promoter. Chromatin immunoprecipitation showed reduced binding of these transcription factors, at least STAT4, to the mutant promoter.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) reported that their proband had not responded to cyclosporine A or oxymetholone. He was started on romiplostim at 4.4 years of age and had a rapid trilineage response, with no further bleeding, infections, or transfusions over 6.5 years of follow-up. Both of his sibs also responded to romiplostim. The brother achieved platelet counts of 30 to 100 x 10(9)/l and remained transfusion independent over 6.3 years. The authors noted that hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is not expected to be effective in patients with THPO mutations.

paragraphs.text: In 2 Micronesian sibs with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2013) identified a homozygous c.112C-T transition in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg38-to-cys (R38C) substitution in the receptor-binding domain. Excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide, the substitution is designated R17C. The sibs' heterozygous parents and a heterozygous sib had reduced platelet counts. In silico modeling predicted that the extra cysteine may disrupt disulfide bonding among the 4 conserved cysteines of the receptor-binding domain. Media containing the mutant THPO had a 2- to 3-fold reduced ability to sustain proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells, consistent with a partial loss-of-function allele.
